subject: Leftover short-call token amortization across invoice cycles
messages:

Subject: Question on short calls / leftover tokens on last invoice

Hi Tessa / Marissa,

Quick question as we review the June invoice draft: several of our integrations make a lot of short inference calls (under 60 tokens generated) that don’t individually hit the minimum billing quantum. On the invoice we see a column for "unbilled partials" and then what looks like a carryover amortization line. Can you confirm:

- Does Redwood aggregate partial-call usage within the billing period to reach the per-call minimum, or are partials rounded up individually?
- If a partial doesn't meet the minimum by month-end, do you carry it forward to the next invoice and amortize across the next cycle, or is it forfeited/credited?

We want the final contract language to explicitly state how these are handled so procurement and finance can sign off. Attached the invoice excerpt and a sample call log.

Thanks,
Jordan Park
Senior Platform PM
Acme Retail

Subject: Re: Question on short calls / leftover tokens on last invoice

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear examples. Short answer: we do clustering within the billing window and then apply a small amortization policy for residuals, but the wording in the contract needs to be explicit. Long answer below and I’ve also looped Marissa (billing) to confirm the sample numbers.

How it currently works (production behavior):
- Within a single billing period (monthly), partial calls are aggregated per-API-key + model variant. We maintain a running partial-token buffer and aggregate until the configured quantum is met.
- If, at the end of the billing period, a given buffer for a key+model contains leftover tokens under the quantum threshold, we carry those forward as a negative balance against the same key in the next billing period and amortize them over the following invoice as an "unbilled residual" line rather than treating them as a hard credit or loss.
- Carryforward is only within the next invoice cycle (one month); if still unconsumed after the subsequent cycle we apply a final rounding policy that either credits up to the customer (if above a threshold) or writes off the micro residual (policy threshold currently $0.50 equivalent).

Practical implications:
- Customers with a high volume of microcalls will effectively see aggregation and will rarely pay for tiny per-call minimums repeatedly.
- For low-traffic keys, a small number of leftovers can either be amortized into the next invoice or dropped per the threshold above.

I’ve attached an internal summary (amortization-math.pdf) and exported a CSV of the invoice lines you highlighted (example-invoice-line.csv). Marissa — can you confirm the write-off threshold and whether we show the carryforward as a negative line or an "unbilled residual" line on the invoice?

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Sales (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Question on short calls / leftover tokens on last invoice

Jordan — thanks for the sample. I pulled the live invoice lines. Confirming the behavior and adding the exact policy numbers we use today.

Policy (current production + invoicing UI):
1) Aggregation window: calendar month (aligned with invoice period). Aggregation keyed by customer org + API key + model SKU.
2) Minimum billing quantum: 25 token-equivalent for the SKU in question. Partials are aggregated until 25 tokens are reached.
3) Carryforward treatment: leftover partials after aggregation are reported as an "unbilled residual" line item on the invoice with a negative quantity shown against the pending aggregation bucket. That residual is automatically applied to the next invoice as a reduction to the billed quantity (not as a credit balance).
4) Final resolution policy: if after the subsequent invoice the residual remains below the absolute dollar threshold of $0.50 USD, we auto-write-off the residual and the invoice system will show a final "micro-residual write-off" note. If it's >= $0.50 it remains as a credit or reduction until consumed.

Example (from your sample-calls.csv):
- May usage aggregated to 24.1 tokens for key X => shows as 0.9 token residual on May invoice (unbilled residual).
- June aggregation consumes the 0.9 residual when key X has new usage; the reduction shows on June invoice as "applied residual from May".

Next steps:
- If you need contractual language, we can propose a clause that spells out aggregation window (monthly), minimum quantum (25 tokens), carryforward (1-cycle), and write-off threshold ($0.50). If Acme prefers a longer carryforward window or no write-offs, we can price-protect that as a small premium.

Karthik — can you run the arithmetic for a 12-month amortization scenario and show the cost delta if we extend carryforward to 3 cycles (penalty/premium)? I’ll draft suggested contract text once we have the numbers.

—Marissa
Senior Billing Analyst
Redwood Inference

Marissa/Tessa/Jordan — ran a quick model on the premium impact if Acme wants carryforward extended to 3 invoice cycles (instead of 1) and if we waive the $0.50 write-off threshold for the pilot. Assumptions: ACME monthly microcall volume ~ 4.2M microcalls, average residual per microcall (after aggregation) ~ 0.018 tokens, current price per token-equivalent = $0.00008.

Scenarios (annualized):
A) Default (1-cycle carryforward, $0.50 write-off): net incremental cost to Redwood (expected) ~ $2,300/year (operational amortization only).
B) Extended (3-cycle carryforward, no write-off): expected incremental cost ~ $18,500/year.
C) Extended + contract guarantee (we guarantee consumption within 3 cycles): would need a premium of ~0.12% on token pricing for the ACME account to neutralize expected cost.

Recommendation: offer a 3-cycle carryforward as a paid add-on (annualized premium 0.12% on token price) or include it in Enterprise tier deals > $X/month. For the immediate PO, propose the standard 1-cycle wording. If Acme asks, we can offer a pilot: 3-cycle carryforward for 90 days at no charge to show impact, then convert to paid add-on.

Jordan — if you want the 90-day pilot we can add it to SOW and mark it as a limited-time concession. Tessa/Marissa — I attached a spreadsheet with the math; we should confirm final premium and draft contract language.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Manager, Pricing Operations
Redwood Inference
